## What you will learn

Find a protein's membrane topology, inspect a bound drug in a structure, and compare gene expression across tissues. Then make two plots in an R Markdown report. This module builds on [membrane structure](../membrane-structure/lec.qmd), [transporters and pumps](../membrane-transport/lec.qmd) and [ion channels](../ion-channels/lec.qmd). **ELO 2, 9.**

Work through these short pages in order:

1. [In the browser: topology, structures and variants](browser.qmd) — about 90 minutes.
2. [In R: tissue expression and membrane topology](report.qmd) — about 90–120 minutes.

## Before you start

No database accounts are needed. You need R, a working R Markdown installation, and the packages below. Install packages once in the R console, outside the report:

```r
install.packages(c("rmarkdown", "knitr", "ggplot2", "jsonlite"))
```

If R Markdown is new, read the [five-minute introduction](../bioinfo-protein-atlas/report.qmd#r-markdown-in-five-minutes).

Download the [student report](bioinfo-membrane-proteins.Rmd) and put it in a new folder. Create a `data` subfolder and save these files there, keeping their names:

- [UniProt membrane features](data/uniprot-features-2026-11-18.csv).
- [GTEx tissue medians](data/gtex-medians-2026-11-18.csv).
- [UniProt provenance](data/uniprot-provenance.json) and [GTEx provenance](data/gtex-provenance.json).

The report can fetch current data; set `use_snapshot <- TRUE` to work from these saved datasets without internet access. Browser activities still need the websites. A failed API request falls back to the supplied snapshot and records that choice in the report.

## Sources

UniProtKB release 2026_04 and GTEx v8 data were downloaded on 2026-11-18. Links to source records and interpretation tasks are on the browser page; API addresses and data provenance are on the report page. [Data credits](../credits.qmd#bioinfo-membrane-proteins).
